textbook-canaliculi.note: One set of fine channels connecting lacunae; this point is not an entire trabecular strut.

textbook-central-canal.note: Longitudinal canal within an osteon; target marks the channel around the vascular bundle.

textbook-diaphysis.note: Representative point on the shaft; the diaphysis is an extended region.

textbook-endosteum.note: The thin lining of the medullary cavity; the target is on the inner surface, not on the periosteum.

textbook-epiphyseal-plate.note: Growing-bone cartilage plate; this is a developmental teaching diagram rather than an adult 3D skeleton feature.

textbook-epiphysis.note: Representative point within the expanded proximal end.

textbook-lacunae.note: One osteocyte-containing lacuna, shown as a small elongated space in the trabecular matrix.

textbook-metaphysis.note: Representative point in the transition between the epiphysis and diaphysis.

textbook-nutrient-foramen.note: Opening where nutrient vessels enter the shaft, shown at the source leader endpoint.

textbook-osteon.note: Representative point within one complete concentric structural unit, outlined by the source.

textbook-perforating-canal.note: Transverse channel carrying vessels across adjacent osteons; target marks the channel around these vessels, not a separate vessel name.

textbook-trabeculae.note: Representative point in the magnified trabecular section; see the accompanying broader inset for the network.

textbook-sigmoid-sulcus-of-temporal-bone.note: Table6.2 names this feature as an example of a line or sulcus. The source table defines the vocabulary but does not depict the exact marking; this is a cited terminology context, not a validated spatial target.

textbook-temporal-lines-of-parietal-bone.note: Table6.2 names this feature as an example of a line or sulcus. The source table defines the vocabulary but does not depict the exact marking; this is a cited terminology context, not a validated spatial target.

textbook-alveolus.note: The alveolar process contains the tooth sockets (alveoli). Teeth obscure most of their sockets in this source view; use this as anatomical context and terminology review, not an exact socket-location test.

textbook-anterior-cranial-fossa.note: Reference point on the floor of this extended depression, not its complete boundary.

textbook-anterior-fontanelle.note: Developmental fibrous gap in the newborn skull, not an adult bony foramen.

textbook-body-of-mandible.note: Representative point on the extended horizontal body.

textbook-calvaria.note: Reference point on the cranial roof; the calvaria extends over several bones.

textbook-condylar-process-of-mandible.note: Reference on the complete ascending condylar process; the articular mandibular condyle is only its head.

textbook-cranial-base.note: Reference point on the skull floor; the complete cranial base includes multiple bones.

textbook-cranial-cavity.note: Reference point within the intracranial space; this is not a bony surface landmark.

textbook-foramen-lacerum.note: Reference point at the opening in a dry skull. In life, the foramen is largely filled with cartilage; the internal carotid artery passes over its superior aspect rather than traversing the cartilage-filled hole.

textbook-foramen-ovale-of-the-middle-cra.target: Foramen ovale of the middle cranial fossa

textbook-hypophyseal-fossa.note: The depression within the larger sella turcica, not the entire saddle-shaped sella.

textbook-infratemporal-fossa.note: Deep space inferior to the arch and medial to the mandibular ramus. The ramus obscures much of the space in this intact lateral skull, so this is a context reference only.

textbook-lateral-pterygoid-plate.note: Lateral lamina of the pterygoid process; source shows the paired medial/lateral plates.

textbook-medial-pterygoid-plate.note: Medial lamina of the pterygoid process.

textbook-middle-cranial-fossa.note: Reference point on the floor of this extended depression.

textbook-nasal-cavity.note: Reference point within the anterior nasal aperture; not the entire posterior extent of the nasal cavity.

textbook-nasal-septum.note: Reference point on the bony septum; the complete septum includes perpendicular ethmoid plate, vomer and anterior cartilage.

textbook-nasolacrimal-canal.note: The fossa for the lacrimal sac lies on the anteromedial orbital wall. The nasolacrimal canal descends from this region to the inferior nasal meatus; the complete canal is not exposed in this anterior source view. No guessed canal pin is shown.

textbook-olfactory-foramina.note: Many tiny openings pierce the cribriform plate beside the crista galli. This source shows the plate but does not clearly resolve a separately verified hole. The plate and its multiple openings are distinct concepts; no whole-plate dot is graded as an individual foramen.

textbook-orbit.note: Reference point inside the bony orbit, a shared cavity made by seven bones.

textbook-paranasal-sinuses.note: The frontal, maxillary, sphenoid and ethmoidal air spaces form a distributed group. The source schematic shows their regional relationships; no single point stands for the entire group.

textbook-petrous-ridge.note: Representative point on the superior ridge of the petrous portion; the ridge and the whole petrous region are different extents.

textbook-posterior-cranial-fossa.note: Reference point on the floor of this extended depression.

textbook-posterior-fontanelle.note: Developmental fibrous gap in the newborn skull.

textbook-superior-nuchal-line.note: Representative point on the ridge; trace its full course in the source.

textbook-supraorbital-margin.note: Representative point on the upper orbital rim.

textbook-temporal-fossa.note: Broad depression on the lateral skull superior to the zygomatic arch. The point gives regional context, not a bounded surface outline.

textbook-temporal-process-of-the-zygomat.target: Temporal process of the zygomatic bone
textbook-temporal-process-of-the-zygomat.note: Zygomatic contribution to the arch; distinguish it from the zygomatic process of temporal bone.

textbook-zygomatic-arch.note: Representative point on the arch; the arch is formed by temporal and zygomatic contributions.

textbook-anterior-sacral-foramina.note: One opening of the anterior series; distinct from the posterior sacral foramina.

textbook-base-of-sacrum.note: Representative point on the broad superior end of the sacrum.

textbook-bifid-spinous-process.note: Reference on one prong of the bifurcated spinous process; not all cervical vertebrae have the same morphology.

textbook-inferior-articular-process.note: The projection bearing an inferior facet; not the complete intervertebral joint.

textbook-posterior-sacral-foramina.note: One opening of the posterior series; distinct from the anterior foramina.

textbook-sacral-canal.note: Superior opening of the canal; not the entire canal course.

textbook-sacral-hiatus.note: Inferior opening at the termination of the sacral canal.

textbook-sacral-promontory.note: Anterior-projecting superior margin of the sacrum; belongs to axial skeleton although viewed within pelvis.

textbook-superior-articular-process.note: The projection bearing an articular facet; the facet surface and the whole process are different extents.

textbook-superior-articular-process-of-t.target: Superior articular process of the sacrum
textbook-superior-articular-process-of-t.note: Process bearing the superior articular facet; the whole projection differs from its joint surface.

textbook-transverse-costal-facet.note: The vertebral facet for the rib tubercle, not the tubercle on the rib itself.

textbook-transverse-sacral-ridges.note: One transverse line of fusion between adjacent sacral vertebral bodies.

textbook-vertebral-arch.note: Representative point on the posterior arch formed by pedicles and laminae; not a single separate bone.

textbook-vertebral-foramen.note: One vertebral opening; stacked foramina together contribute to the continuous vertebral canal.

textbook-body-of-rib.note: Representative point on the rib shaft distal to the angle.

textbook-costal-groove.note: The costal groove runs along the inferior internal aspect of the rib and accommodates the intercostal neurovascular bundle. This source view shows posterior articulation and rib angle but does not clearly expose the complete groove. No guessed groove pin is shown.

textbook-sternal-angle.note: Reference point at the manubriosternal junction; the ridge is extended across the sternum.
